3.40.betting_forecast: 8/11 Hearts And Spades, 4/1 Last Round, 8/1 Heartbreak Weather, 9/1 Asphalt Cowboy, 10/1 Irina's Path, 14/1 Squire Ohara,
3.40.spotlight_verdict: Ian McCarthy and Rob James teamed up to win with Fountain House (won this race last year) on Tuesday, and can take this with HEARTS AND SPADES who looks a cut above the others on points form. Last Round looks the better of the Elliott pair. Heartbreak Weather is the most appealing of the remainder. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: Winner of two hunter chases on good ground over longer distances at Downpatrick; placed in three points since last October; has struggled in hunter chases at Down Royal and Fairyhouse, and concerning that he was pulled up in this race last year when a 5-1 chance; blinkered.
Has completed only once from six starts in points; remote sixth behind Dacman on latest; can be ruled out.

Pulled up in a bumper two years ago on only start for Willie Mullins; has made gradual improvement in points; opened his account at Tattersalls Farm after remote third behind Heartbreak Weather at Monksgrange; more on his plate now.

Sprang a 25-1 surprise in this race in 2023, his only success from 67 appearances on the track, placed eight times; moderate fifth here in 2024 and pulled up in last year's edition; should be better for a recent point run, but up against it at the age of 13.
Weak form over hurdles and in points; remote fifth behind Heartbreak Weather at Monksgrange in March; the trainer of the 2018 winner also runs Hey Sir.

Sprang a 25-1 surprise in this race in 2023, his only success from 67 appearances on the track, placed eight times; moderate fifth here in 2024 and pulled up in last year's edition; should be better for a recent point run, but up against it at the age of 13.

Respectable form in points this season, notably when second to the subsequent Ladies' Cup winner Fountain House in a trial for this event here; in touch when falling three out at Ballycahane; made a couple of slight mistakes on the way to Monksgrange win.

Outstanding form in points this term, winning six from seven; no disgrace in neck Portrush defeat to Winged Leader, the most prolific Irish points winner ever (37 wins); raced a bit too keenly when only third (beaten favourite) on hunter chase debut at Cork; can repeat stable's 2025 win with the talented Fountain House, an easy winner under Rob James here on Tuesday.
Trainer won this with Alpha Male in 2018, but this one appears to have little chance; pulled up in this race last year and finished behind three of these rivals in a hunt race here two months ago.
Twice placed in maiden hurdles in 2024; weak form last year; good enough to win a recent maiden point at Castletown-Geoghegan, but the form does not amount to much.

Looked quite promising in points last season; below that standard this term; two poor runs since third here in February, when 16l behind runner-up Heartbreak Weather; same connections as 2024 winner Private Ryan.
Two wins in points early in her career; three-figure odds when pulled up here 12 months ago; remote fourth in a recent point.

Won soft-ground point early last year; fair placed form in a pair of hunter chases on good ground last season, one of them won by Asphalt Cowboy; career-best when a 10l winner of a maiden hunter chase at Limerick last Christmas; sights lowered now after hunter chase runs at Thurles and Naas.

Form has gone downhill since second of four finishers behind Fountain House in this race 12 months ago; saddle slipped when rider was unseated last time; previously last of six behind Hearts And Spades at Tyrella.

4.15.betting_forecast: 5/2 Its On The Line, 3/1 Wonderwall, 5/1 Panda Boy, 7/1 Lets Go Champ, 8/1 Hunters Yarn, 10/1 Wrappedupinmay, 12/1 Asian
4.15.spotlight_verdict: Last year's Cheltenham winner WONDERWALL has had a relatively light campaign and may atone for a below-par Festival run in March. Its On The Line has a flawless record in this race and a remarkable, if frustrating, Cheltenham record. Not at his best at Aintree, he rates a major threat back at this venue. Panda Boy has the beating of a couple of key rivals, and Lets Go Champ produced a terrific effort at Aintree that puts him firmly in the mix. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: Four wins over hurdles; has never won a chase; point-to-point form nowhere near good enough.

Promising early in his career for this stable and initially did well for Willie Mullins, winning twice over hurdles and taking fourth in the Supreme Novices'; also placed in good company over fences; has prospered again in points this season; Journey With Me got a better jump at the last to beat him in a hunter chase at Cork last month.

Looked a smart prospect when beating Its On The Line at Down Royal in December 2024; disappointing overall since then, except for an 18l Fairyhouse win last season; remote third in the same race this year; poor completion rate this season; risky.

Twice runner-up in hunter chases last season; beaten favourite both times; beat a subsequent winner handily in a maiden point in February; had little trouble justifying favouritism in a maiden hunter chase at Downpatrick; smart long-term prospect, this may come a year too soon.
Four wins from five starts in points; won a Down Royal hunter chase in March; big step up in class now.

In the form of his life when winning four races over fences for Christian Williams in 2021; had been running well enough in points before profiting from the mishaps of fancied rivals to win at Fairyhouse.

Three-time bumper winner; three wins over jumps for Willie Mullins before losing his way; has prospered in points this term for his original trainer, winning three from four; beaten favourite on all three hunter chase starts, second to Panda Boy at Naas, second to Lets Go Champ at Gowran, going well when falling three out at Fairyhouse.

Won this for the third time last year; contrasting profile in the Cheltenham equivalent now having finished second in four consecutive years; easily the best of the Irish this year, with Panda Boy fifth and Wonderwall (his conqueror last year) seventh; never got competitive in the Aintree Foxhunter, a rare blot on his record; has his quirks, but as tough as they come.

Won a competitive handicap chase at the 2024 festival for Henry de Bromhead (2m4f, good to yielding); hunter chase victory over Hunters Yarn at Gowran Park showed that he retains considerable ability; confirmed that impression when beating all bar star hunter Barton Snow at Aintree; goes well for Sophie Carter.

7-14 in points and a five-time winner on the track; has often run well in races at this level, notably when second to Its On The line in this race in 2024 and third in the 2025 Aintree Foxhunter; no match for Panda Boy at Thurles in January; readily outpointed by Wonderwall at Dromahane 19 days ago
Veteran has been competing quite effectively in points; however, could manage only a moderate fourth in an incident-packed Fairyhouse race won by Five Star Getaway.

Smart staying handicap chaser in his prime; has found a new lease of life, winning two hunter chases at Thurles (beat Lifetime Ambition by 9l) and Naas (beat Hunters Yarn by 4l); might have found the ground a bit too quick when finishing fifth behind Barton Snow at Cheltenham; could play a featuring part.
More than three years since his last racecourse win; pulled up in the hunter chase won by Panda Boy at Thurles in January; held by Asian Master on Cork running.

Has run only three times since beating Its On The Line at Cheltenham last season; winner of points at Dromahane in November and 19 days ago, that recent display providing reassurance after a disappointingly lifeless Cheltenham defence; leading contender for the stable that has dominated the point-to-point scene this season.

Four wins in five races in points, the defeat inflicted by Hunters Yarn at Moig South last autumn; that rival seemed to be getting the upper hand when they both fell three out in the Fairyhouse race won by Five Star Getaway; useful second-string for champion-elect points trainer.

4.50.betting_forecast: 8/11 Dinoblue, 9/4 Only By Night, 11/2 Spindleberry, 12/1 Kala Conti, 25/1 Broomfield Bijou, 66/1 Sophia Rose.
4.50.spotlight_verdict: It is hard to get away from the claims of the top-rated DINOBLUE. She's very well treated by the race conditions and she looked as good as ever when beating Only By Night and Spindleberry at Cheltenham last time. Kala Conti was moving ominously well when coming down at Aintree last time and if that hasn't left a mark, she could challenge for a place. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: 1-12 over fences and rated 125; hasn't won since scoring in a mares' chase at Wexford in July 2024; difficult to see her losing run ending in this company.
horses.trainer: Raymond P Fitzgerald J W Hannon
horses.breeding: b m Walk In The Park - Aure Antique

horses.spotlight_comment: High-class mare has won eleven of her 20 starts over fences, including this race last year; as good as ever this season and won the Mares' Chase at Cheltenham on latest (Only By Night runner-up, Spindleberry fourth); top-rated here and best treated by race conditions; the one to beat.
horses.breeding: ch m Doctor Dino - Blue Aster

horses.spotlight_comment: Talented hurdler made a bright start to her chasing career, winning two mares' chases at Cork (beat Kargese easily in the second one); fine second in the Grade 1 Scilly Isles at Sandown behind Sixmilebridge but took a heavy fall when moving into contention at Aintree last time; if that hasn't left a mark she could go well, though she's not well treated by race conditions.
horses.breeding: b m Karaktar - Rolibie De Vindecy

horses.spotlight_comment: Last year's Arkle runner-up is 4-8 over fences; won a Naas Grade 3 on her seasonal return in November; disappointed in a Grade 1 at Leopardstown a month later but back on song when chasing Dinoblue home in the Mares' Chase at Cheltenham; big player again here.
horses.breeding: b m Affinisea - Leyhill

horses.spotlight_comment: Sligo maiden hurdle winner is 0-6 over fences and rated 103; out of her depth in this company.
horses.trainer: Race & Stay Racing Club G Cromwell
horses.breeding: ch m Mount Nelson - Grangeclare Gold

horses.spotlight_comment: Won first five chase starts, including two Listed mares' chases and a Grade 1 at Fairyhouse in April last year; came unstuck upped to 3m in the Irish Gold Cup and no match for Dinoblue or Only By Night at Cheltenham latest; badly in at the weights here and looks up against it on these terms.
horses.breeding: b m Policy Maker - Sapphire Rouge

5.25.betting_forecast: 11/2 Funiculi Funicula, 7/1 Shuffle The Deck, 17/2 Noble Park, 10/1 Kish Bank, 12/1 Kiss Will, Port Joulain, 13/1 Spread Boss
5.25.spotlight_verdict: With Willie Mullins saddling eight, Paul Townend's choice Funiculi Funicula must have a big chance. However, preference is for the Ted Walsh-trained SHUFFLE THE DECK with this better ground and longer trip to suit. A couple of those in behind Noble Park at Newbury have won since, and the British raider holds a good chance. Spread Boss Ted and Kiss Will are just two of the others with very plausible claims in an open race. [Denis Harney]

horses.spotlight_comment: Maiden hurdle winner built on previous chasing promise with a 2l win at Kelso in February (2m5f, good to soft) in a four-runner field; this is a different challenge altogether and needs to improve again in first-time cheekpieces.
horses.trainer: Simon Munir & Isaac Souede S Crawford
horses.breeding: b g Soldier Of Fortune - Molly's Affair

horses.spotlight_comment: Useful hurdler won his chasing debut at Fairyhouse (2m, soft) in January, staying on well; soundly beaten over 2m1f here next time (heavy); gave 5lb to Raglan Road when 7l behind that rival at Down Royal last time (2m5f, good to yielding); more needed.
horses.breeding: gr g Milan - The Crown Jewel

horses.spotlight_comment: Second in last season's Jack Richards Handicap Chase at Cheltenham (2m5f, good to soft, 125-1); won a Kilbeggan beginners' chase in June, 2.25l in front of You Oughta Know; left two disappointing efforts behind when a creditable fourth of seven at Cheltenham in October (3m1f, good); back chasing after moderate hurdles run last time and Kennedy rides for the first time.
horses.trainer: K Haughey & Kieran T Byrne D Budds
horses.breeding: b g Jukebox Jury - Adira

horses.spotlight_comment: One of eight for trainer; dual bumper and maiden hurdle winner in 2024; runner-up on chase debut at this venue (2m7f, heavy) before falling four out back here next time; failed to justify 5-6 favouritism at Naas (2m4f, soft to heavy) last time when a 0.5l second behind Spread Boss Ted; now enters handicap chase company.
horses.trainer: John J Brennan & David Flynn W Mullins
horses.breeding: b g Soldier Of Fortune - Hear The Thunder

horses.spotlight_comment: Three hurdle wins including at this track; mixing chasing with hurdles after returning from an absence this season; not a bad run in the Martin Pipe when eighth; needs a bit more; declared for 4.15 on Thursday.
horses.breeding: b g Fame And Glory - Oscar Ladensa

horses.spotlight_comment: The fact Townend picks him from the stable's eight runners is a very big positive; maiden hurdle winner placed in Grade 1 novice company at Aintree last term (2m4f, good); beaten favourite in opening two chase runs before making the breakthrough at Cork (2m1f, yielding) last time, when defeating Wingmen by 0.75l; big player with further improvement plausible.
horses.trainer: Michael A O'Riordan & Seamus Hennessy W Mullins
horses.breeding: br g Storm The Stars - Fun Run

horses.spotlight_comment: Has taken well to chasing this term, winning a 2m2f Clonmel beginners' (heavy) and good late headway for fourth behind Romeo Coolio in a Leopardstown Grade 1 (2m1f, yielding) over Christmas; good attitude when runner-up in a Down Royal novice chase in January (2m1f, yielding to soft); okay run when fifth in a Listed Naas handicap (2m4f, heavy) when last seen.
horses.breeding: b g Kayf Tara - Ten Times Better

horses.spotlight_comment: Useful hurdler won his chasing debut at Fairyhouse (2m, soft) in January, staying on well; soundly beaten over 2m1f here next time (heavy); gave 5lb to Raglan Road when 7l behind that rival at Down Royal last time (2m5f, good to yielding); more needed.
horses.breeding: gr g Milan - The Crown Jewel

horses.spotlight_comment: Scudamore (GB) Derek Fox 25-1 132 131 150 Unsuccessful in three chase runs in first half of the season, including when well beaten on handicap debut at Musselburgh (2m5f, good to soft, 9-4 favourite); reverted to hurdles with a poor effort in the Morebattle after wind surgery but better effort when sixth at Aintree last time (2m4f, good to soft); returns to chasing now.
horses.breeding: b g Jet Away - Jet Setting Fiona

horses.spotlight_comment: One of two for trainer; point/hurdle/bumper winner was a beaten favourite in two beginners' chases before making immediate impact on handicap chase debut at Leopardstown (3m1f, yielding) off 118; never travelling when pulled up next time at Naas (2m4f, heavy); back on track when run down late on at Navan (3m, soft to heavy); up 4lb for that effort but in the mix.
horses.breeding: b g Mount Nelson - Surtee Du Berlais

horses.spotlight_comment: British runner; commenced chase career with good-ground wins at Hereford and Lingfield; below par in two subsequent starts but bounced back to form with a 4.25l win at Newbury last time (2m4f, good to soft) and a few of those in behind have won since; up 7lb now but ground and distance look like his optimum.
horses.trainer: M Buckley & A Speelman N Henderson (GB)
horses.breeding: b g Walk In The Park - Cove

horses.spotlight_comment: British runner; hurdles winner is now rated 22lb higher over fences after back-to-back wins on soft ground over 2m4f at Sandown; decisive victor of five-runner contest in January and justified 4-6 odds last month when seeing off two rivals; this big field is new for him, but he's in fine form.
horses.breeding: br g Soldier Of Fortune - Coco Des Champs

horses.spotlight_comment: Three-time winning hurdler in 2024; immediate winner over fences at Galway (2m2f, yielding) before following up in a Cork Grade 3 novice (2m4f, good to yielding) next time, with You Oughta Know 2.75l behind in second; poor effort in Grade 1 company in November at Fairyhouse; never on terms after a bad mistake at the fifth at Cheltenham when last seen; tough task conceding weight all round.
horses.breeding: b g Ol' Man River - Curragh Na Gold

horses.spotlight_comment: First reserve; three-time hurdles winner has been beaten a long way in five chase starts this season, including in novice handicaps the last twice; unseated at the fourth at Wexford last time; 10lb lower mark in this sphere and has won on good ground, so there are positives if returning to form.

One of eight for trainer; point and bumper winner two seasons ago and won his maiden hurdle here early last year (2m4f, heavy); much improved display, compared to poor opening chase start here, when successful at Fairyhouse in January (2m1f, yielding), beating a better-fancied stablemate; had the run of things when third of five in a Navan Grade 3 novice last time.
horses.breeding: b g Cokoriko - Apple's Noa

horses.spotlight_comment: Hurdles winner was soundly beaten in opening three chase runs; well backed when winning a Down Royal rated novice chase last time (2m5f, good to yielding); likely capable of more.
horses.trainer: John P McManus H De Bromhead
horses.breeding: b g Soldier Of Fortune - Akiliyna

horses.spotlight_comment: Dual hurdle winner last season on good-to-yielding; safely held in quality beginners' chases; 3-1 favourite for handicap chase debut at Fairyhouse (2m1f, soft) last time when kept on for third, 11l behind the winner; step up in trip should help, as should this better ground; chance.
horses.breeding: b g Walk In The Park - A Country Girl

horses.spotlight_comment: British runner is a three-time hurdles winner who has taken well to fences this season; built on positive chase debut when scoring from the front at Sandown (2m4f, soft) in March; not given an easy lead at Newton Abbott and jumping lacked fluency when last of the four runners (2m5f, good); easy lead could be difficult to find once again in this big field.
horses.trainer: Tom Bond J & A J O'Neill (GB)
horses.breeding: b g Doyen - Like A Miller

horses.spotlight_comment: One of eight for trainer; bumper and dual winning hurdler had no chance when a faller on chasing debut at Navan in January (3m, soft to heavy) and was a moderate fourth of seven here next time (2m7f, heavy); much better when seeing off better-fancied stablemate Ballygunner Castle at Naas by 0.5l last time (2m4f, soft to heavy); in the mix on handicap chase debut.
horses.breeding: b g Yorgunnabelucky - She's The Lady

6.00.betting_forecast: 8/13 King Rasko Grey, 7/1 You Proof, 8/1 Kiely's Place, 10/1 Jalon D'Oudairies, 12/1 Saint Baco, 14/1 Echoing Silence, Lord
6.00.spotlight_verdict: Willie Mullins has won the last five renewals of this race and KING RASKO GREY, who was an impressive winner of the Turners at Cheltenham, is the one to beat for him here. It looks pretty open otherwise and Jalon d'Oudairies, Echoing Silence and Lord Byron, the sole 4yo in the race, can fight it out for the places. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Tramore maiden hurdle winner sprang a surprise when winning a four-runner Thurles Grade 3 novice (21.5f, yld-sft) in February; that form has taken a few knocks since, however, and Paul Townend has jumped ship; more needed up in grade.

Point-to-point and bumper winner; won first two starts over timber, a Cork mares' maiden hurdle (2m4f, yielding) and a Listed mares' hurdle here (2m3f, heavy); mid-field in Grade 2 mares' novice at Cheltenham on latest (2m1f, good); return to further should suit and gets weight from the boys; could challenge for a place.
horses.breeding: b m Doyen - Taipers

horses.spotlight_comment: Point-to-point and dual bumper winner; off the mark over hurdles on penultimate start when making all for a dominant win at Naas (18.5f, sft-hvy); 3m may have stretched him when well beaten in the Albert Bartlett last time; may do better dropped back in trip; place claims.
horses.breeding: b g No Risk At All - Ukalee

horses.spotlight_comment: Smart bumper performer (including a win here); sole success from four runs over timber came in a Navan Grade 3 novice in November; beaten twice since, including in a novice hurdle at Navan on latest, and has plenty of room for improvement in the jumping department.
horses.breeding: ch g Masked Marvel - Escort'Chance

horses.spotlight_comment: Point-to-point winner won on his Rules' debut in a Clonmel maiden hurdle (19.5f, sft-hvy) in February; sent off at 11-2 but made no impression upped in grade at Fairyhouse on latest (20.5f, yld-sft); needs to improve plenty on that, but he's lightly raced so that's not impossible; hood goes on.

Didn't win a bumper but has proved a much better hurdler; comfortably landed a Limerick maiden hurdle in December; close third in 2m Grade 1 novice at the DRF in February; stepped up in trip and won the Turners in impressive fashion at Cheltenham; preferred by Townend and the one to beat.
horses.breeding: b g Galiway - Imaginary Move

horses.spotlight_comment: British raider; 4yo is 0-5 over hurdles but far from disgraced the last twice when a 3.5l fifth of 20 in the Triumph at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) and a 6.5l fourth of 12 in the Grade 1 Mersey Novices' Hurdle at Aintree; gets weight all round and rated 141, so definite place chance on the figures.
horses.breeding: b g Camelot - Shamooda

horses.spotlight_comment: French recruit won a Navan maiden hurdle (2m, sft-hvy) on return from long absence in December; has come up well short in three starts since; beaten 26l in a Grade 1 at Naas; beaten when falling at the last in the Turners; beaten 20l in Fairyhouse Grade 2 latest; much more needed.
horses.breeding: b g Muhtathir - Al Doha

horses.spotlight_comment: Runner up in sole point-to-point; off the mark on hurdles' debut at Limerick in December (21.5f, sft-hvy); soundly beaten in Grade 2 novice at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yld-sft) on latest; early days still but new tongue-tie needs to eke out lots more.

6.40.betting_forecast: 4/9 Lossiemouth, 6/1 William Munny, 8/1 Golden Ace, 11/1 Wilful, 14/1 Anzadam, 40/1 Absurde, 50/1 Glen Kiln.
6.40.spotlight_verdict: Willie Mullins landed the past three runnings of this contest with State Man, but this time it is LOSSIEMOUTH's turn to shine. She justified connections' decision to line up in the Champion Hurdle when comfortably landing her tenth Grade 1 success and it will be a shock if she doesn't maintain her unbeaten record at this venue. William Munny hasn't been seen since runner-up in last season's Supreme but would be in the mix if at his peak. Anzadam has a place chance if putting it all together, while County Hurdle winner Wilful needs to improve again now entering Grade 1 company, but is thriving. [Denis Harney]

horses.spotlight_comment: One of three for trainer; dual-purpose sort who has run creditably in the last three Melbourne Cups (rated 107 on the Flat); 2024 County Hurdle winner was well below his best in that race this season back from a break (2m1f, soft); improved display at Cork when 3.25l behind Ndaawi (16.5f, yielding); a good bit to find with Lossiemouth even if running to his rating, which he hasn't done so far this term.
horses.trainer: H O S Syndicate W Mullins
horses.breeding: b g Fastnet Rock - Incroyable

horses.spotlight_comment: Enjoyed a standout season, highlighted by landing Grade 3 honours at Naas in January (2m, heavy); has been found out upped to Grade 1 level twice this term, 19l behind Lossiemouth in the Morgiana Hurdle (16.5f, soft to heavy) and no chance when unseated at the last in the Hatton's Grace (2m4f, yielding to soft); below his best in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 last time; hard to see him being involved.
horses.breeding: b g Famous Name - Lucy Stone

horses.spotlight_comment: Fortuitous winner of the 2025 Champion Hurdle (same story in this season's Fighting Fifth); could only manage fifth when attempting to retain her crown (9.75l behind Lossiemouth); posted another solid effort in the Aintree Hurdle last time when fourth (2m4f, good to soft); return to 2m should suit, cheekpieces go on and she was second in this contest last year (good) but may need further luck to increase Grade 1 haul.
horses.breeding: b m Golden Horn - Deuce Again

horses.spotlight_comment: One of three for trainer; prolific and highly talented mare justified decision to line up in this year's Champion Hurdle when adding a tenth Grade 1 win to her tally (14-18 overall) in good style; had both Anzadam and Golden Ace well behind her on that occasion; 3-3 at this venue, including when 19l in front of Glen Kiln in this season's Morgiana Hurdle; this looks easier than Cheltenham and she's ground-versatile; shock result if she doesn't win.
horses.breeding: gr m Great Pretender - Mariner's Light

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive 7yo won a competitive Ascot handicap in December (15.5f, good to soft) and was second in a valuable Windsor handicap next time (2m, soft); posted career-best effort in the County Hurdle last time, keeping on well to win by three lengths (2m1f, soft); has course form after filling the second spot in a festival handicap here last season; enters Grade 1 company now and will need a good fist of improvement again, but he's clearly thriving.
horses.trainer: Mrs Fitri Hay J & A J O'Neill (GB)
horses.breeding: br g Westerner - Shuil Milan

horses.spotlight_comment: Unseen since taking the runner-up spot behind Kopek Des Bordes in last season's Supreme Novices' Hurdle (2m, good to soft); that was just his fourth hurdles start after placing in his opening two maiden hurdles at Leopardstown and Fairyhouse and comfortably winning a Listed novice hurdle (soft) over this C&D before his Cheltenham run; contender if running to his best but it would be a huge performance to win this after 416 days off.
horses.breeding: b g Westerner - Court My Eye

7.10.betting_forecast: 7/1 Pioneer Pete, 9/1 Saveforarainyday, 10/1 Arslan, Dee's Lady, Spirou, 12/1 Chichester Park, Spy, 14/1 Whimsy, 15/1
7.10.spotlight_verdict: Harry Derham was 'dumbfounded' when SPIROU managed to win at Newbury on stable debut after 852 days off the track and he could be up to defying top weight with improvement likely. A change of tactics, compared to his maiden victory, didn't work on handicap debut for Arslan but he's worth another chance off this mark. The hood worn for Saveforarainyday's easy maiden hurdle win is back on after she disappointed last time. Pioneer Pete must back up his wide-margin maiden hurdle win. [Denis Harney]

horses.spotlight_comment: Winner of an ordinary Thurles maiden hurdle in December (2m, yielding); outpaced on handicap debut at same venue before satisfactory third in a Leopardstown novice hurdle next time (2m, soft to heavy); didn't improve for step up in trip in Down Royal handicap last time (2m5f, yielding); point-to-point win came on good ground.
horses.breeding: b g Yorgunnabelucky - Spangle Island

horses.spotlight_comment: First reserve; 1-15 over hurdles but placed several times; capable of more than what he showed at Plumpton (2m, good) last time but others preferred.
horses.breeding: gr g Dark Angel - Back In The Frame

horses.spotlight_comment: Point and bumper winner has been absent since winning a Downpatrick maiden hurdle in September (2m2f, yielding); took second off a 15lb lower mark in a big-field Galway handicap in July prior to his win (2m6f, good); player if ready to rock.
horses.breeding: b g Muhaarar - Confidential Lady

horses.spotlight_comment: French heavy-ground bumper winner; well beaten in three maiden hurdles and tailed off at Fairyhouse on handicap debut last time (2m, yielding to soft); an interesting jockey booking.
horses.breeding: b g Kendargent - Nistabelle

horses.spotlight_comment: Never outside top three in three starts over hurdles, including a Sligo maiden hurdle win (2m2f, good to yielding) in October; more needed now entering handicap company.
horses.trainer: Loose Chippings Syndicate P G Fahey
horses.breeding: b m The Irish Rover - Mafaaza

horses.spotlight_comment: Authoritative Wetherby maiden winner (2m, good) last month on his fifth start over hurdles; needs to back it up now entering handicap company; one for the shortlist.
horses.trainer: Furlong Friends J & A J O'Neill (GB)
horses.breeding: b g Frontiersman - Premier Blanc

horses.spotlight_comment: Flat winner got off the mark immediately over hurdles when winning a Navan maiden hurdle last year (2m, heavy); well beaten in a Naas novice contest next time before some consistent Flat efforts; unseen since tailed off at Naas back over hurdles on final start for Michael O'Callaghan in November; needs to bring his best.
horses.breeding: b g Make Believe - Not My Way

horses.spotlight_comment: Well backed to win third maiden hurdle start following the addition of a hood at Limerick (2m, heavy); won impressively that day, but the headgear was left off on handicap debut at Fairyhouse when well beaten (2m, yielding to soft); hood goes back on now and Mark Walsh stays loyal.
horses.breeding: b m Crystal Ocean - Timolin

horses.spotlight_comment: French hurdle winner surprised his trainer when winning on stable debut back from an 852-day absence at Newbury in March (2m1f, good); nudged up 2lb for that and could defy top weight with improvement likely.
horses.breeding: ch m Charming Thought - Cape Victoria

horses.spotlight_comment: Record of 1-19 over timber; three-time winner on the Flat has placed in two starts in that sphere since falling over hurdles at Leopardstown in March; recent form suggests she's fit and healthy but poor strike-rate over hurdles is off-putting.

Debut Bellewstown bumper winner in 2024 (2m1f, good to yielding); showed promise in a couple of maidens last season but returned from a 380-day absence for his first handicap at Fairyhouse (2m, yielding to soft) and was tailed off; may do better with that run under his belt; cheekpieces on.
horses.trainer: R S Brookhouse H De Bromhead
horses.breeding: b g Belardo - Creese

horses.spotlight_comment: Three hurdles wins, the latest at Downpatrick in July over 2m3f (good); pulled up after making mistakes over fences when last seen at Downpatrick in August; may need this first run back.
horses.breeding: b g Soldier Of Fortune - Alfa Belle

7.40.betting_forecast: 5/2 Cityofblindinlites, 7/2 Premier Division, 7/1 Thinkitdontjinxit, 15/2 Muckanagh Lough, 17/2 Largy Star, 9/1 Heldam, 14/1
7.40.spotlight_verdict: Martin Brassil won this race in 2024 and his CITYOFBLINDINLITES (nap) should be able to uphold Leopardstown form with Premier Division. Largy Star is another one to consider, as is Muckanagh Lough. Thinkitdontjinxit should improve for this longer trip and the selection's stablemate Gonewild is interesting at likely bigger odds. The market can guide as to the prospects of the Willie Mullins' trio. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: 22-1 and never landed a blow on debut at Fairyhouse in November; not easy to make a case for on that evidence.

Solid form on debut at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting, finding just The Mourne Rambler too good (Premier Division third, the fourth and fifth have both won since); hung to the right that day so this track should suit; leading claims if seeing out this longer trip (mixed messages in pedigree).
Outran odds of 66-1 to finish a 7.75l third on debut in a Clonmel bumper (2m3f, soft); should improve for that experience but will need to find more to figure here.
Related to a couple of winners but was never involved on debut at Down Royal in December when a 40-1 shot; tongue-tie now goes on.
Very modest form in three bumpers and unseated at the fourth on hurdles debut at Tramore on latest; would be a surprise winner.

Homebred Mahler gelding; dam placed 1m 2yo-2m1f Flat (inc AW; RPR 75) and 2m/2m5f hurdle winner, half-sister to 6f winner Marble Bar, out of Listed-placed 7f 2yo winner (stayed at least 1m4f); shrewd connections have won this race before, so market check advised.

One of three for yard; promise on debut in a hot maiden hurdle (2m, yielding) at Leopardstown in December that has thrown up plenty of winners; weakened late when beaten 11.5l into third in a 2m3f Cork bumper (yielding) after a 100-day break in first-time tongue tie (retained); may have needed that and could go well.

Point-to-point winner; sent off the 15-8 favourite but well held by Cityofblindinlites on their meeting at Leopardstown in December; failed to justify short odds when an 8.5l third of four at this venue in February (2m, heavy); can't dismiss given who trains him, but others have stronger form.

Crystal Ocean mare; half-sister to eight winners inc Don Poli (high-class 2m4f-3m1f hurdle/chase), Debece (useful bumper and 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Politesse (useful bumper and 2m-3m hurdle/chase); dam 2m winner; respected source, well bred and worth a market check.

Attracted a bit of market support on debut (40-1 into 14-1) at Down Royal in December but completely tailed off; probably capable of better, but hard to fancy on that effort on first start for new yard.

Sent off at 18-1 on debut at this venue in 2023 and ran a fine race to finish a 3.75l third (Fleur In The Park second) for Ray Cody; now in the care of Willie Mullins and while a 933-day absence is off-putting, any market moves for this half-brother to Killultagh Vic should be noted.

One of three for yard; stayed on for an 18l third on debut in a 2m bumper at this meeting last year; this longer trip should suit on that evidence, but stable has stronger claims with Gonewild and Cityofblindinlites.

2-3 in point-to-points; remote second on Rules' debut in a Naas bumper (18.5f, heavy); got much closer when a 5.75l third in a Fairyhouse maiden hurdle on latest in first-time tongue tie (retained) and that form has been boosted by the runner-up; player.
Modest form in both starts in point-to-points; by a top sire and dam a Listed bumper winner but needs to improve plenty to feature here.
Placed in one of three starts in point-to-points; cost E110,000 as a 3yo and related to two bumper winners, but major step forward required on Rules' debut.

Ordinary point-to-point form but fine effort on second start under Rules when 1.75l second of 9 at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting (2m4f, yielding); beaten 0.5l on debut for this yard in a Limerick bumper (19.5f, sft-hvy) when didn't get the clearest of runs; solid chance.
Has shown minor promise in three of her four bumper starts, including when a 12.5l fourth of 7 in a Listed heat at Gowran when last seen in October; needs to improve again to make an impact here.
Ordinary form in two bumper runs for Fergal O'Brien, the latest at this meeting last year when beaten 82l; has joined a top yard but needs to leave those previous efforts well behind.

Beaten favourite when a 4l third of 11 at Fairyhouse; solid run when a 5.5l third behind The Mourne Rambler and Cityofblindinlites at Leopardstown; place claims again upped in trip, but not certain to turn the tables on Cityofblindinlites.
50-1 and pulled up before the last on debut in a Gowran maiden hurdle in November; seems safe to rule out.

Expensive purchase has yet to live up to his price tag; best effort a 7.5l second of 18 in a Fairyhouse maiden hurdle (2m4f, yielding) on penultimate; heavy defeat in a Gowran bumper (2m2f, heavy) on latest; others appeal more.

Bought for 185,000GBP after winning a Ballycrystal point-to-point by 8l; runner-up in two bumpers at Thurles in February-March, both over 2m on soft and soft-to-heavy ground and shaped like further would suit in the latest one; not discounted up in trip.
Austrian School gelding; dam unraced half-sister to useful 2m2f-3m hurdle/chase winner Bally Longford, out of unraced sister to smart Irish hunter chaser Stay In Touch; likely best watched on debut.
